title: Bags, cases, gloves and caps
summary: How to carry cartridges, how to carry and transport a gun (soft slip and hard case) and why Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting shooters use gloves and a cap.

body.html: You need many cartridges at a ground, and they are heavy: 25 cartridges weigh about a kilogram. For the day's supply there is a cartridge bag: sturdy, with a wide strap and a stiff base, holding several boxes. For a single round a belt cartridge pouch or the vest pockets are handier.

Carry a separate bag or pocket for empty cases. In both disciplines empties go into the bin on the stand where there is one, and shooters with semi-automatics pick up their ejected cases when they leave. Do not leave cases in the grass: it is a matter of tidiness and respect for the place.

A gun slip is a light zipped soft case for carrying the gun around the ground and between stands. Some grounds require the gun to be in a slip, or open and unloaded, when you are away from the stand. Rules for carrying a gun: Carrying a gun: ground, car and home.
Never put a loaded gun into a slip. Unload it and check both chambers first.

A hard case protects the gun when you travel by car and especially by air. Flying usually requires a sturdy lockable case, and cartridges travel separately under the airline's rules (see Flying with a gun). Transport laws differ between countries, so check the law of your country and of your destination.

Shooting gloves are thin, so you can still feel the trigger. They improve your grip, especially in heat when palms sweat, and in the cold. After a long series the barrels get hot, and a glove on the hand that holds the fore-end protects against burns. Many shooters wear a glove on one hand only.

A shooting cap with a peak shades your eyes from the sun, keeps rain off your glasses and gives a little protection from small fragments falling from above. The peak should not be too long, or it will hide high targets.

key_points.html: A cartridge bag for the day; a pouch or vest pockets for a round.
Collect empty cases and put them in the bin, not in the grass.
A soft slip at the ground, a hard case for travel; only an unloaded gun goes into a slip.
Gun transport laws differ between countries, so check them.
Thin gloves for grip and hot barrels; a cap with a modest peak.

did_you_know.html: A few boxes of cartridges in a bag weigh several kilograms, so on a course many experienced shooters carry only what they need until the next refill point.

quiz.q: What is a hard case for?

options.text: To protect the gun during travel
To rest the gun on while shooting
To keep cartridges cool in summer

quiz.explain: A case protects the gun in a car or plane; transport rules depend on the country.

quiz.q: What must not go into a gun slip?
quiz.explain: The gun is unloaded and checked before it goes into a slip.

options.text: So that they wear out faster
So you can still feel the trigger
So that they dry faster in rain

quiz.explain: A thick glove stops you feeling the trigger and the fore-end.
